Samir —

Thanks for the numbers and the sample prompts — super helpful. Quick high-level cost framing based on your current 60M/month baseline: 

Scenario A — Hosted pay-as-you-go (typical Redwood hosted model):
- 8k-capable model (good for ~70% of requests): list price roughly $1.20 / 1M tokens.
- 32k-capable model (for the ~25% mid-size requests): list price roughly $1.60 / 1M tokens.
- 128k-capable model (fall-back for ~5% research): list price roughly $2.50 / 1M tokens.
- Blended run-rate at your current mix (~70/25/5) => ~ $1.40 / 1M tokens => ~$84k/month (estimate).

Scenario B — Dedicated / committed capacity (monthly reserved commit + discounted unit rates):
- Estimated unit range: $0.60 - $0.95 / 1M tokens depending on commit level and model family.
- For a 12-month commitment sized to your current 60M/month baseline we can get close to your $1.00 / 1M target (likely in $0.85 - $0.95 range) and better if you commit to growth.

Operational notes / suggestions:
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeated prompts or retrieval-heavy flows we frequently see 10-30% token savings on completions.
- Mixed routing: route short/latency-sensitive calls to smaller, cheaper variants; route retrieval-heavy calls to 32k variants; route research jobs to dedicated 128k instances (on-demand or reserved compute) to avoid paying high unit costs across the whole fleet.
- Quantization & model sizing: we can evaluate lower-precision variants for the non-research traffic — typically 10-25% unit-cost reduction with minimal quality loss for classification/QA workloads.

Next steps:
1) I’ll put together a short line-item estimate (hosted vs committed) and a recommended routing/quantization plan tuned to your sample prompts — attaching a draft (redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf).
2) Confirming the follow-up: Oct 14, 10:00am PT works for our side (Jordan + Rishi will join). I’ll include a short slide with break-even points for commit levels.

If you confirm the Oct 14 slot I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda. Thanks again — happy to tighten the numbers after we see the full profiling CSV.
